messages:
Priya: quick check — we're planning a rollout for the search model override. Current setup: org default has `feature_flags.model_quantized = true`, project `nlp-search` wants a 10% canary, and the route `/search/instant` needs a temporary model override to `mpt-q4` for latency testing. Which scope wins at runtime (org/project/route/model)? Also: are route overrides able to bypass project canaries? cc @jamie @marco

Jamie: route-level explicit override should win at evaluation time. precedence we use is: route > model (route-attached model) > project > org. route override won't bypass a traffic split unless it's explicitly marked as a `force` override. normal route overrides are still subject to split evaluation.

Marco: to add — on Dedicated vs Hosted: routing uses model compatibility + availability. If `mpt-q4` isn't available in the target pool, runtime will try the route's compatible fallback (e.g., `mpt-q3` quantized variant) and emit a fallback event. That means route > project precedence still holds, but the selected model might be substituted at execution time.

Sasha: quick example of how the canary interacts — assume project canary = 10% (user assignment by hashed user_id). A route override that is NOT `force` will only affect requests in that 10% bucket. If you want everyone hitting the route to see it, set `route_override.force = true` (but need approvals).

Priya: can you show a config snippet for what you mean? want to include in rollout runbook.

Jamie: pasted quick schematic:

```
{
  "org": { "model_quantized": true },
  "project": {
    "id": "nlp-search",
    "canary_percent": 10
  },
  "route": {
    "path": "/search/instant",
    "override": {
      "model": "mpt-q4",
      "force": false,
      "meta": { "requested_by": "priya", "ttl": "24h" }
    }
  }
}
```

Jamie: resolution algorithm (high level): 1) determine audience (canary split) 2) check for explicit route override; if present and not forced, apply only if user in audience 3) choose runtime model, substitute compatible fallback if unavailable 4) emit audit/log event with resolution path

Sasha: infra check command you can use locally:

`infractl flags resolve --route "/search/instant" --user-id 12345 --project nlp-search`

sample (toy) output:

```
resolved: route_override
applied_model: mpt-q4 -> not available in us-west -> fallback mpt-q3-q4a
audience: project_canary (10%) -> user 12345 in_bucket: true
events: [audit:route_override_applied, fallback:substituted_model]
```

Emily: security/audit note — please ensure route overrides that set `force=true` include `approved_by` and `jira_ticket`. Also TTL by default should be <= 48h unless reviewed. We should block force overrides to prod without approval.

Jamie: easy guardrail: require schema fields `approved_by` + `jira` for any `force=true`. infra will enforce at API schema level and infractl will reject pushes missing those fields. We can also add a pre-validation webhook to the console for UI flows.

infra-bot: :warning: policy-check failed: pushing route override with `force=true` to `prod` without `approved_by` metadata is disallowed. See /policies/route-overrides for details.

Marco: ops caveat — when fallback happens (model substituted), the route override still counts as applied for metrics/rollout. Make sure ML evals compare final model outputs, not just the declared override.

Priya: thanks — action items:
- Jamie: add schema enforcement for `force` overrides (approved_by, jira, ttl)
- Sasha: add infractl example + doc snippet to rollout runbook
- Marco: ensure fallback events bubble to metrics and evals
- Emily: add TTL default policy and prod block for force overrides

Priya: tagging this thread as the canonical short Q&A for the `/search/instant` rollout. I'll follow up with a PR for the runbook and the RFC link. :thumbsup:
